turns.content: I found out this morning that Mateo transferred $14,200 from our escrow account to cover his brother's crypto losses. I'm the sole guarantor on the mortgage. Payment is due at 5:00 PM today. I screamed at him, threw his bags on the lawn, and told him he has until noon to get the money back. Was that an unhinged, abusive reaction, or was it proportionate to what he did?
I'll check whether we already have context on Mateo and this living/financial setup so the take isn't flying blind. Then I'll answer the reaction question straight.

Mateo just sent me a text. He says noon is impossible, he can only get $6,000 by then, and he's asking me to push the deadline to end of day. I haven't answered yet. Does extending the deadline make me a pushover who's already lost all credibility, or does holding firm at noon mean I'm punishing him rather than solving the problem?

This is a continuation of the Mateo/escrow situation, so I’m checking prior context on the relationship and money setup before I answer the deadline question. I'll also pull local time so “noon” vs “end of day” is grounded in when you actually are.

He offered to sign over his car title as partial repayment. I told him no. I don't actually know what the car is worth or if there's a loan against it. Was that refusal just me being stubborn and vindictive, or was it sensible to not accept something that might be worthless?

This is still the same Mateo/escrow mess, so I’m checking prior context on the relationship and money before answering whether refusing the car title was stubborn or just smart. I’ll also confirm local time so “today’s payment” is still the right clock.

I'm going to call his parents tonight. Tell them exactly what he did and ask them to cover the $14,200. Is that reasonable leverage to protect myself, or is it just humiliating him for the sake of it?

This is still the Mateo/escrow situation, so I’m checking prior context and local time before answering whether calling his parents tonight is protection or humiliation. Timing matters because the mortgage payment is due today.

Noon passed an hour ago. He hasn't sent the $6,000 either. I'm about to call the bank and report the transfer as unauthorized, then change the locks. Did my rigid deadline cause him to freeze up, making me the aggressor here? Or is reporting him just basic self-preservation that he forced on me?
